title: Repo-internal facts that change the harness-install plan
trigger: Implementing or re-planning docs/plans/2026-09-19-harness-native-install-plan.md, or touching src/cli.js, src/mcp/server.js, .grok-plugin/, or .grok/ for distribution work.
behavior_delta: (1) .grok-plugin/marketplace.json and .grok/hooks/dd.json + .grok/rules/dd.md already exist in this repo since its first commit, untested — the marketplace.json's plugins[0].source uses {"type":"local","path":"./"}, which does not match Grok Build's documented schema (a plain source string); fix it, don't recreate it, and don't assume the project-level .grok/hooks/dd.json is new work — it already runs the same code path Claude Code's project-level hooks/hooks.json does. (2) src/mcp/server.js has no exported entry point — it's a top-level-await script that runs fully on import (confirmed by reading lines 8-27); any CLI subcommand that needs to start the MCP server must do a plain side-effecting `await import('./mcp/server.js')`, not import a named function. (3) src/cli.js's main() currently calls openStore() unconditionally before checking the command; any new subcommand that shouldn't open a store for the *current* directory (install, mcp) must branch before that call — and if a plan adds two such subcommands across separate tasks, the task that first restructures main() this way must land before any task whose subcommand depends on that restructuring (Codex's `install` branch before OpenCode's `mcp` branch, in this case).
what: (1) .grok-plugin/marketplace.json and .grok/hooks/dd.json + .grok/rules/dd.md already exist in this repo since its first commit, untested — the marketplace.json's plugins[0].source uses {"type":"local","path":"./"}, which does not match Grok Build's documented schema (a plain source string); fix it, don't recreate it, and don't assume the project-level .grok/hooks/dd.json is new work — it already runs the same code path Claude Code's project-level hooks/hooks.json does. (2) src/mcp/server.js has no exported entry point — it's a top-level-await script that runs fully on import (confirmed by reading lines 8-27); any CLI subcommand that needs to start the MCP server must do a plain side-effecting `await import('./mcp/server.js')`, not import a named function. (3) src/cli.js's main() currently calls openStore() unconditionally before checking the command; any new subcommand that shouldn't open a store for the *current* directory (install, mcp) must branch before that call — and if a plan adds two such subcommands across separate tasks, the task that first restructures main() this way must land before any task whose subcommand depends on that restructuring (Codex's `install` branch before OpenCode's `mcp` branch, in this case).
why: Found 2026-09-19 while writing the implementation plan: the first draft ordered the OpenCode task before the Codex task, which would have made the OpenCode task's own steps reference a src/cli.js shape (the install branch, the pre-openStore() branching) that didn't exist yet. Caught during the plan's required self-review, before any code was written.
